results.reason: Issue 1 identifies MSA §3.2 nationwide exclusivity for all warehousing/freight/delivery, contrasts with Term Sheet §4.1 NYC-metro last-mile only, and proposes narrowed replacement language.

Issue 2 identifies §11.3 carving Customer's §10.2 indemnity out of the caps while Provider's §10.1 stays capped at 12-month fees, explains the one-sided unlimited exposure, and recommends striking the carve-out and making exceptions mutual.

Issue 3 identifies DPA §9.1 Delaware law and Wilmington courts, notes the conflict with MSA §18.1 New York, states that the DPA prevails under §2.3, and recommends conforming the DPA to the MSA's New York law and forum.
Issue 4 identifies the 3-year auto-renewal with a 15-day window, explains the lock-in, and recommends 1-year renewals with any-time notice at least 90 days before expiry.
Issue 5 identifies SOW §8.2 free assignment by Provider versus MSA §17.4 restricting only Customer, explains the competitor and unvetted-carrier risk, and recommends a mutual consent clause.
States that the DPA prevails over the MSA and the MSA prevails over the SOW.
States that the cap is the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.
Memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner, and each issue has Where, Why it matters, and Recommended fix sections.
Issues are listed in order of importance, and Section V lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
Concludes that the Delaware clause controls and that the documents are not consistent on governing law.
States that the exclusivity clause contradicts and far exceeds the Term Sheet.
